title: Which one is bigger?
goal: Compare anything with two prefixes that never change — **по-** for "more" and **най-** for "most" — a system far simpler than English.
bekal: putting the definite article on the **най-** form

dialogs.title: Диалог — Sofia, Plovdiv and Jakarta
dialogs.intro: Ivan and Ani compare cities. Notice that **по-** and **най-** are always written with a hyphen and always carry the stress.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Which city is bigger — Sofia or Plovdiv?
lines.literal: which — city — is — bigger — Sofia — or — Plovdiv?

lines.speaker: Иван:
lines.id: Sofia, of course. It's the biggest city in Bulgaria.
lines.literal: Sofia, understands — itself. she — is — biggest-the — city — in — Bulgaria.

lines.speaker: Иван:
lines.id: Plovdiv is older and calmer. Sofia is more modern.
lines.literal: Plovdiv — is — older — and — calmer. Sofia — is — more-modern.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: In Jakarta there are far more people.
lines.literal: in — Jakarta — there-is — much — more — people.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: About ten million. Eight times more than Sofia.
lines.literal: about — ten — million. eight — times — more — than — Sofia.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Much hotter. The coldest day there is warmer than the warmest day here in winter.
lines.literal: much — hotter. coldest-the — day — there — is — warmer — than — warmest-the — day — here — during — winter-the.

lines.speaker: Иван:
lines.id: Then winter will be the hardest thing for you.
lines.literal: then — winter-the — will — to-you — be — hardest-the — thing.

notes: **По- and най- never change.** Bulgarian has no irregular comparatives like *good / better / best*. It simply attaches two prefixes to any adjective: *голям → по-голям → най-голям*. One system, no exceptions.

⚠️ **The hyphen is required, not decoration.** *По-голям* with a hyphen means "bigger"; *по голям* without one means nothing. The same goes for *най-*. It is the most common spelling mistake among learners — and among Bulgarians themselves in text messages.
⚠️ **По- and най- always carry the stress.** *ПО-голям*, *НАЙ-голям*. The adjective itself loses its main stress. If you say it without stressing the prefix, your comparison won't be heard.
**For "than", use от**, the same preposition as "from": *София е по-голяма от Пловдив.* If what follows is a clause, use *отколкото*: *По-лесно е, отколкото мислех.* (It's easier than I thought.)

**The най- form takes the definite article** — which makes sense, because "the most" is always specific. *Най-големият град* (the biggest city), *най-хубавата песен* (the nicest song). The article sits on the adjective, following the rule from Unit 12.
⚠️ **Много has an irregular comparative: повече.** Not *по-много*. Its opposite, *по-малко* (less, fewer), is regular. This is the only exception you need to memorize in the whole unit.
**To strengthen a comparison, put много in front**: *много по-топло* (much warmer), *много по-добре* (much better). It works exactly like "much" in English.
**Вече means "already" and goes before the verb.** *Вече разбирам* (I understand now), *Вече е късно* (it's already late). Its opposite is *още не* — not yet: *Още не разбирам.*

grammars.title: Three degrees, two prefixes
body: Works for adjectives and adverbs alike, with no difference in form.
after: The adjective still agrees with its noun as usual: *по-голям град*, *по-голяма къща*, *по-голямо дете*, *по-големи къщи*. The prefix *по-* changes nothing about that agreement.
⚠️ Don't mix up **по-добър** (adjective: better) and **по-добре** (adverb: better, in a better way). *Този филм е по-добър* (this film is better) versus *Говоря по-добре* (I speak better).

grammars.title: Comparing two things
body: Four patterns that cover almost every everyday comparison.

head: Pattern
Example
English
rows: София е най-големият град в България.
Sofia is the biggest city in Bulgaria.
A е толкова X, колкото B
Пловдив е толкова хубав, колкото София.
Plovdiv is as nice as Sofia.
A не е толкова X като B
Не е толкова студено като вчера.
It isn't as cold as yesterday.
There are more people than yesterday.

after: The third and fourth patterns use the pair **толкова … колкото** — "as … as". For a more casual comparison, use **като** (like): *Той е висок като баща си.* (He is as tall as his father.)

blocks.text: Notice how many use a fleeting vowel in the masculine — *дълъг / дълга*, *нисък / ниска*, *лесен / лесна*, *топъл / топла*. If you're unsure of the feminine, drop the last vowel before the final consonant, then add **-а**.

⚠️ **Добър (good) is not the same as хубав (nice).** *Добър човек* means a good-hearted person; *хубав човек* means a good-looking one. Swapping them won't stop the conversation, but your compliment may miss the mark.
The most useful exercise, and the one you'll need most often — because every Bulgarian will ask you about your country. Here is Ani's version.

head: Bulgarian
English
rows: Индонезия е много по-голяма от България.
Indonesia is much bigger than Bulgaria.
В Индонезия има много повече хора.
There are far more people in Indonesia.
В София е по-студено, отколкото в Джакарта.
It's colder in Sofia than in Jakarta.
Животът в София е по-евтин от живота в Джакарта.
Life in Sofia is cheaper than in Jakarta.
The hardest thing is the winter.
The best thing is the people.

blocks.text: The last row shows something subtle: *най-хубавото нещо* is singular, but the verb is **са** (plural), because what follows is *хората*. Bulgarian makes the verb agree with the part that explains, not the part being explained. English would say "is" here, so just notice it — no need to worry.

blocks.title: Useful numbers for this conversation
items: Bulgaria has about **6.5 million** people and covers about 111,000 km² — roughly the size of Iceland or the US state of Tennessee.
Indonesia has about **280 million** people — more than forty times as many. The sentence: *Индонезия има четирийсет пъти повече хора от България.*

Sofia lies 550 meters above sea level, one of the highest capitals in Europe. The lowest temperature ever recorded in Bulgaria is **−38.3 °C**. Mention that number to anyone from the tropics and watch their face.

exercises.prompt: Form the comparative and the superlative.
Put the words in the right order.

items: This is the nicest city in Bulgaria.
The hardest thing is the winter.

по, от — най — повече — по, от — най
Кой град е по-голям? — София е най-големият град. — Пловдив е по-стар от София. — Много по-топло е. — Най-трудното нещо е зимата.
